commits.pr_body:
## Overview `RocmPlatform`'s automatic backend selection passes `is_turboquant_run` to `_get_invalid_reasons` but not `is_ultraquant_run`, so `--kv-cache-dtype ultraquant_4bit` fails at engine startup on ROCm unless `--attention-backend` is set. This passes the flag in the automatic path too, as the explicit-backend path already does. Related: #54988 (the same fix for TurboQuant), #57057 (UltraQuant backend). Not a duplicate: before opening I searched open and closed PRs and issues for `is_ultraquant_run`, "UltraQuant ROCm", "ultraquant boundary" and the error text below. The only related change is #54988, which fixed the same selection path for TurboQuant only. #67789 (open) fixes a different UltraQuant/TurboQuant bug (prefill fast path) and does not touch backend selection. ## Claims - `ultraquant_4bit` starts on ROCm with automatic backend selection; the boundary layers get a backend whose KV layout UltraQuant can share (TRITON_ATTN on gfx942). - New selection test mirroring the existing TurboQuant one; it fails without the fix and passes with it. - End-to-end regression test through `vllm_runner` (Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B, `kv_cache_dtype="ultraquant_4bit"`, no explicit backend): engine startup fails without the fix and the model answers with it. ## Validation Hardware: 1x MI300X (gfx942), ROCm nightly image `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm` v0.34.1rc1.dev100+gc2cc003c5. The tests were run at that commit (`c2cc003c5`) with this diff applied; the branch is rebased on main `62d538c`, where the same two lines are still missing (`vllm/platforms/rocm.py`, automatic path) and the diff applies unchanged.
Selection test: fails on base, passes with the fix, whole file passes ``` $ pytest -q v1/attention/test_rocm_attention_backends_selection.py -k ultraquant_boundary # base c2cc003c5 E AssertionError: assert is not 1 failed, 89 deselected in 0.39s $ patch -p1 < fix.diff && pytest -q v1/attention/test_rocm_attention_backends_selection.py -k ultraquant_boundary 1 passed, 89 deselected in 0.31s $ pytest -q v1/attention/test_rocm_attention_backends_selection.py 90 passed in 13.89s ```
End-to-end test through vllm_runner: fails on base, passes with the fix (nightly 5aea30579, MI300X) ``` $ pytest -q v1/attention/test_rocm_attention_backends_selection.py -k ultraquant_starts_with_automatic # base 5aea30579 ValueError: No KV cache layout satisfies every supported set: [['LHBNC', 'LBHNC'], ['LBNHC']]. RuntimeError: Engine core initialization failed. See root cause above. Failed core proc(s): {} 1 failed, 89 deselected in 26.97s $ patch -p1 < fix.diff && VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error pytest -q v1/attention/test_rocm_attention_backends_selection.py -k ultraquant_starts_with_automatic 1 passed, 89 deselected in 47.25s $ pytest -q v1/attention/test_rocm_attention_backends_selection.py # tests at 5aea30579 + this test 90 passed in 53.50s ```
End to end: LLM(model="Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct", kv_cache_dtype="ultraquant_4bit", max_model_len=32768) Before (base): ``` (EngineCore pid=342) ERROR 11-26 07:59:24 [core.py:1795] ValueError: No KV cache layout satisfies every supported set: [['LHBNC', 'LBHNC'], ['LBNHC']]. ``` After (this PR), the engine starts and the layer report shows: ``` attention | 4 | TRITON_ATTN | model.layers.[0-1, 26-27].self_attn.attn attention | 24 | ULTRAQUANT [kv_cache=ultraquant_4bit] | model.layers.[2-25].self_attn.attn ``` LongBench (multifieldqa_en / hotpotqa / 2wikimqa, 100 prompts each, ~3.5k tokens, greedy, token F1) then runs: 0.484 / 0.398 / 0.330 at defaults. With #67789 also applied: 0.483 / 0.413 / 0.385, vs bf16 KV 0.487 / 0.414 / 0.399.
Lint: `ruff 0.17.2` (the version pinned in `.pre-commit-config.yaml`) check and format report nothing new on the two changed files compared with main. ## Details Root cause: in automatic selection, `_get_invalid_reasons` only filters boundary-layer candidates for packed-KV runs when told the run is TurboQuant or UltraQuant. With only `is_turboquant_run` passed, UltraQuant runs keep ROCM_ATTN as the first valid candidate for the native-dtype boundary layers. Its layouts (LHBNC, LBHNC) do not intersect UltraQuant's (LBNHC), so the KV cache layout resolution fails at startup. The explicit `--attention-backend` path already passes both flags. The change is 2 lines in `vllm/platforms/rocm.py` plus two tests in the existing ROCm selection test file (a 38-line selection test and a 13-line end-to-end test), so they run wherever that file runs in CI. Limitation: validated on gfx942 only. ---

- Pass attention sinks on the `fp8_ds_mla` branch of `ROCM_AITER_MLA_SPARSE`, so HY4 and HY4 Flash can use an `fp8_ds_mla` KV cache on gfx950
- Opt HY4 Flash's sliding-window layers in to `fp8_ds_mla` on ROCm, as #68365 did on NVIDIA, and drop the ROCm-only BF16 DFly check

HY4 on ROCm was missing three things NVIDIA has, and none of them needed AITER changes. AITER's Triton sparse MLA kernel already takes an attention sink, but vLLM never passed it on the `fp8_ds_mla` path, so `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla` crashed at startup with an assert. GSM8K stays at 96.7% against 96.8% on main. ShardQ is gated by local head count because AITER's kernel already fills its 16-head tile at TP2 and TP4, where ShardQ only added exchange cost (1.15-1.5x slower). commits.pr_title: [Pre-commit][Bugfix] Move torch.cuda check into check_forbidden_strings
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

This PR moves the `torch.cuda` check (RFC #30679) into `check_forbidden_strings.py` and fixes its bugs.

## Changes

- The `torch.cuda`, `torch.cuda.manual_seed` and `current_platform.mem_get_info` rules are now in `CHECK_STRINGS`.
- `tools/pre_commit/check_torch_cuda.py` and its `check-torch-cuda-call` hook are removed.
- The hook now finds `current_platform.mem_get_info()`. Before, this pattern did not find any match.
- The hook now finds all forms of `torch.cuda.device`: a call, a `with` block, or a bare reference.
- The hook now shows all errors in a file, and it ignores text in `#` comments.
- The `cuda_device_count_stateless` rule is removed. It is a legacy API and the old pattern did not find any match.
- `test_regex()` has new cases for the three rules.

**Root cause:** The old patterns ended with `\(\)\b` or `\(\b`. This regex needs a letter or digit after the bracket, so it almost never matches.

## Validation

Commit: `293f739`


commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

The child stack dump that #67605 added for timed out AMD CI tests prints no stacks since Python 3.14 became the default in #68457. `py-spy` 0.4.1 cannot read a 3.14 process, so every dump ends in `stack dump failed`. This pins `py-spy` 0.4.4 for the ROCm test image, adds a fallback without native frames, and fixes the test, which passed without any stack.

## Claims

- With `py-spy` 0.4.4 the dump prints the stacks of the child processes again, including the engine process of a real test.
- When `py-spy dump --native` fails, the plugin now tries `py-spy dump` without `--native` before gdb.
- `test_a_timed_out_test_dumps_the_stacks_of_its_child_processes` can no longer pass without a stack, and in the AMD CI image a new test fails when `py-spy` does not support the running interpreter.

## Validation

**In upstream CI today.** Six `test_vit_cudagraph_image[llama4]` timeouts on MI355 DPX in the last week have no stack for the hung engine, for example https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/105466#01a20eab-6e20-4e3e-ad0d-bb94c14d02f0

```
[amd-ci] test timed out: stacks of 2 child processes
[amd-ci] ---- pid 4604 ppid 2141 (running): VLLM::EngineCore
[amd-ci] kernel wait channels: futex_wait_queue x42, do_epoll_wait x9, 0 x2, hrtimer_nanosleep x2, kfd_wait_on_events x1
stack dump failed: py-spy: exit 1 ['Error: Failed to find python version from target process']
```

**Same plugin on a real engine.** CI image at commit 418af607309d (Python 3.14.10), MI350X, with `--cap-add SYS_PTRACE`, only the `py-spy` on `PATH` differs.

```
pytest -q -s -p amd_ci_fast_exit -o faulthandler_timeout=25 models/multimodal/generation/test_vit_cudagraph.py -k "llama4 and image"
```

py-spy 0.4.1 from the image (this run used `faulthandler_timeout=40`)

```
[amd-ci] ---- pid 158 ppid 32 (running): /usr/bin/python -c from multiprocessing.spawn import spawn_main; spawn_main(tracker_fd=38, pipe_handle=40) --
[amd-ci] kernel wait channels: futex_wait_queue_me x77, ep_poll x9, hrtimer_nanosleep x2, 0 x1, kfd_wait_on_events x1
stack dump failed: py-spy: exit 1 ['Error: Failed to find python version from target process']
```

py-spy 0.4.4

```
[amd-ci] ---- pid 158 ppid 33 (running): /usr/bin/python -c from multiprocessing.spawn import spawn_main; spawn_main(tracker_fd=38, pipe_handle=40) --
[amd-ci] kernel wait channels: futex_wait_queue_me x34, 0 x1
Process 158: /usr/bin/python -c from multiprocessing.spawn import spawn_main; spawn_main(tracker_fd=38, pipe_handle=40) --multiprocessing-fork
Python v3.14.10 (/usr/bin/python3.14)

Thread 158 (active+gil): "MainThread"
    _generate_tokens_from_c_tokenizer (tokenize.py:588)
    getblock (inspect.py:1128)
    getsourcelines (inspect.py:1161)
    JITCallable.__init__ (triton/runtime/jit.py:471)
    JITFunction.__init__ (triton/runtime/jit.py:791)
    ...
1 passed, 57 deselected, 17 warnings in 72.97s (0:01:12)
```

**In upstream CI on this PR.** In https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/105738 `:amd: (MI250) Docker Build Metadata` ran on the image built from this PR, with Python 3.14.10, and `test_py_spy_reads_this_interpreter` passed. `(CPU) Docker Build Metadata` failed in that build, because the CPU image has py-spy 0.4.0 and the two stack checks ran there too. They now run only in the AMD CI image.

**Unit tests**, commit 17919abfbc, dev container with Python 3.12.15, py-spy 0.4.1, ptrace permission and `libamd_ci_fault_trap.so` built in place, because the stack checks run only where that library exists.

```
pytest tests/tools/test_amd_ci_fast_exit.py -q -p no:cacheprovider
14 passed, 16 warnings in 18.79s
```

With a stub `py-spy` first on `PATH` that prints `Error: Failed to find python version from target process` and exits 1, and `-k "test_a_timed_out_test_dumps or test_py_spy_reads"`

| | result |
| --- | --- |
| test from main | `1 passed, 12 deselected, 16 warnings in 4.48s` |
| this PR | `2 failed, 12 deselected, 16 warnings in 4.74s` |

With a stub that prints `Error: Permission denied (os error 13)` this PR gives `1 passed, 1 skipped, 12 deselected, 16 warnings in 4.62s`. Without the library, as in the CPU image, the first stub gives `1 passed, 1 skipped, 12 deselected, 16 warnings in 4.56s`.

## Details

Root cause. `py-spy` enters the ROCm test lock through `ray`, and the lock had it at 0.4.1. Python 3.14 support came in 0.4.2. `requirements/test/rocm.in` now pins `py-spy==0.4.4`, the version I checked, and the `pip-compile-rocm` hook updates the lock. Nothing else in the lock changed.

Why the test did not catch it. The test looked for `hang_in_child` in the output, and the dump also prints the command line of each process. The children were started with `python -c <source>`, so the function names were in the command line. The children now run from files.

The fallback. Two timeouts from Nov 18 and 19, still on Python 3.12, failed in `--native` with `UNW_EINVAL: unsupported operation or bad value` on the hung engine. On a healthy engine `--native` works with 0.4.4, so I could not reproduce that one. A stack without native frames is better than none.

Limitations

- In the one MI250 timeout I found, py-spy reports `Permission denied (os error 13)` for every process, so those pods seem to lack ptrace permission. This PR does not change that, and the stack assertion is skipped when py-spy reports it. The step that runs this test file is on an MI250 pod.
- The new test checks `py-spy` against the interpreter with `py-spy record` on a process it starts itself, which needs no ptrace permission. That ran on an MI250 pod in the CI build above. If a pod forbids that too, the test skips.
- The CUDA and CPU test locks keep `py-spy` 0.4.0, which cannot read Python 3.14 either. `(CPU) Docker Build Metadata` runs this test file on the CPU image, so the stack checks run only in the AMD CI image, where `libamd_ci_fault_trap.so` exists.

Why this is not a duplicate. I searched open PRs and issues for `py-spy`, `amd_ci_fast_exit` and `stack dump`. #68874 uses py-spy in `vllm/utils/watch_dog.py` and does not touch the test image or this plugin.

commits.pr_title: [CI] Skip the global cleanup after kernel tests that skipped themselves
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Skip the global per-test cleanup after kernel tests that skipped themselves. This fixes `(MI355) Miscellaneous Kernels` in AMD CI, which keeps timing out at its 54 min step limit with no failing test ([amd-ci build 15886](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/15886/list?sid=01a2174d-ecbd-471e-b969-21533854541b&tab=output)).

## Claims

On MI355X, 283 self-skipping kernel tests go from 102.53 s to 2.20 s on the same commit.

Tests whose body ran, including xfailed tests, keep the cleanup exactly as before.

No test is removed and no CI timeout is raised. The expected saving for `(MI355) Miscellaneous Kernels` is 16 to 18 min, from about 54 min to about 36 min.

## Validation

All runs on commit 23b2463644, MI355X, ROCm, from `tests/`, with `HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0`. "Before" is the same tree with the original `tests/kernels/conftest.py`.

Skipped tests:

```bash
pytest -q kernels/test_fp32_router_gemm.py kernels/test_bf16_skinny_gemm.py \
  -k "test_fp32_activation or test_cute_selected_shapes"
```

```
before: 283 skipped, 1367 deselected in 102.53s (0:01:42)
after:  283 skipped, 1367 deselected in 2.20s
```

Passed tests still get the cleanup (`--durations=0`, teardown entries summed):

```bash
pytest -q kernels/test_apply_repetition_penalties.py --durations=0
```

```
before: 131 passed in 49.94s, 131 teardowns, 44.7s total
after:  131 passed in 51.71s, 131 teardowns, 43.2s total
```

A probe test file covering each outcome confirmed the cleanup runs after a passed test and after an xfailed test, and not after a test that skips from its body. A test skipped by a mark never sets up the fixture, as before.

## Details

**Root cause.** The autouse `cleanup_fixture` in `tests/conftest.py` calls `cleanup_dist_env_and_memory()` after every test. Its full `gc.collect()` costs about 0.6 s per test early in a shard and grows to 1 to 2 s late in a long run. Many kernel tests skip from their body on unsupported hardware (for example CUDA-only CuTe DSL paths), after the fixture is already set up, so they pay this cost for no work. In build 15886, pytest finished with 2143 passed, 1559 skipped and 0 failed in 3218 s against a 3240 s step budget, and the skipped tests accounted for about 1114 s. The step timed out in 5 of the last 19 runs.

**Change.** `tests/kernels/conftest.py` records a skipped call report in the item stash and overrides `cleanup_fixture` to skip the cleanup for that test. This follows the existing subdirectory override in `tests/lora/conftest.py`. It still honours `should_do_global_cleanup_after_test`, so `tests/kernels/moe/`, which turns that off and cleans on entry instead, is unaffected.

**Scope.** The change is limited to `tests/kernels`. The tests there that set up state before skipping release it themselves (context managers or plain tensors). Outside `tests/kernels` some tests create an `LLM` before skipping, so a global version would need a separate review.

AI assistance was used for this PR.

commits.pr_title: [CI][ROCm] Speed up the block-quant reference matmul in kernel tests
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

`native_w8a8_block_matmul` in `tests/kernels/quant_utils.py` is the pure torch reference for the block quantized fp8/int8 GEMM and MoE tests. It ran one small matmul per (N tile, K tile) pair. I changed it to run one matmul per K tile across all of N, which keeps the same accumulation order and makes the reference several times faster.

## Claims

Measured locally on MI300X (gfx942), `kernels/moe/test_block_fp8.py` goes from 386 s to 120 s, `kernels/moe/test_block_int8.py` from 105 s to 10.5 s and `kernels/quantization/test_block_fp8.py` from 97 s to 68 s. I will add the actual savings per CI group once the CI runs finish.

No test, tolerance or kernel code is changed, and all tests pass with the same pass and skip counts as before.

## Validation

All runs are on MI300X (gfx942). Timings were measured on main `632ba4f90c`. After rebasing onto `23b2463644` I reran `kernels/moe/test_block_int8.py` with the change applied and it still passes (83 passed).

Before:
```
kernels/moe/test_block_fp8.py           174 passed, 169 skipped in 385.51s
kernels/moe/test_block_int8.py          83 passed in 104.72s
kernels/quantization/test_block_fp8.py  221 passed, 562 skipped in 96.59s
```

After:
```
kernels/moe/test_block_fp8.py           174 passed, 169 skipped in 119.74s
kernels/moe/test_block_int8.py          83 passed in 10.50s
kernels/quantization/test_block_fp8.py  221 passed, 562 skipped in 67.81s
```

To check that the reference itself did not move, I ran the three files with a pytest plugin that computes both the old and the new function on every call and compares them. For int8 all 2060 calls are bit identical. For fp8 the MoE file made 3766 calls and 0.0011% of the output elements differ, and the quantization file made 125 calls with 0.0003% differing. The largest difference is below one bf16 ulp at the tensor's scale (0.45% of the tensor max).

I also recorded how close every `assert_close` in the two MoE files gets to its tolerance, as max(|out - ref| / (atol + rtol * |ref|)). The value is unchanged for all 255 checks and the worst case stays at 0.670. In the quantization test the kernel's rel_diff against the reference is about 2e-7 against a limit of 1e-3, and the change moves it by at most 8e-9.

I also checked edge cases against the old function: empty and 3D inputs, N or K not divisible by the block, non square blocks, int8 and fp16/fp32 outputs. All results are identical and invalid inputs raise the same assertions.

## CI

CI build [106020](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/106020) passes on all affected steps: MI300 DPX MoE Kernels, MI300 DPX Quantization Kernels, MI355 DPX FP8 MoE Kernels, MI355 AITER FP8 GEMM and MoE, L4 MoE Kernels, H100 DeepGEMM Kernels, B200 Kernels and B200 FusedMoE Layer Kernels. 

The per file times below are compared against main build [105939](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/105939) for MI300 DPX, and against the daily build [105800](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/105800) and build [105900](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/105900) for MI355 DPX, which is not run on every main build. Pass and skip counts are the same as before.
```
MI300 DPX  kernels/moe/test_block_fp8.py           301 s  ->  117 s
MI300 DPX  kernels/moe/test_block_int8.py           83 s  ->   14 s
MI300 DPX  kernels/quantization/test_block_fp8.py  188 s  ->  169 s
MI355 DPX  kernels/moe/test_block_int8.py      170 / 95 s  ->   15 s
```


## Details

With N=9216 and K=7168 the old loop issues 4032 matmuls per call, and the MoE reference calls it twice per expert, so the tests were bound by kernel launches. In one profiled `test_w8a8_block_fp8_fused_moe` case the reference took 27 s of 32 s, while the fused MoE kernels under test took 0.06 s.

A single matmul over dequantized operands would be faster still, and the same scale expansion with `repeat_interleave` is already used in `tests/models/common/specialized_decode/reference.py`, `tests/models/glm5next/test_mega_moe.py` and `vllm/model_executor/kernels/linear/scaled_mm/cpu.py`. I didn't use it here because it sums in a different order than the kernels being tested, which accumulate per K tile (`accumulator += tl.dot(a, b) * a_scale * b_scale` in `fused_moe.py`). When I tried it, the tolerance margin got tighter in 15 MoE tests, the largest move being from 0.446 to 0.584. Looping over K tiles keeps the per tile products, scales and accumulation order. The remaining last bit differences come from the GEMM library choosing a different algorithm for a 128 by N product than for a 128 by 128 one. Int8 is always exact because the per tile sums fit in fp32.

The trade off is memory. Each K tile now holds two M by N fp32 temporaries, which adds about 0.6 GiB per call for the largest shapes these tests use.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][CI] Use an fp32 lm_head for granite4_h in test_pp_tied_word_embeddings
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fix intermittent failures of `distributed/test_pipeline_parallel.py::test_pp_tied_word_embeddings[granite4_h]` (added in #67349) on the `:amd: (MI250) Pipeline + Context Parallelism` step by running Granite's `lm_head` in fp32 with `hf_overrides={"head_dtype": "float32"}`, the same one-line change #58945 and #66486 made for the OLMoE LoRA tests.

## Claims

- `granite4_h` no longer flakes on MI250: 22/22 local runs pass, while main failed 6 times in CI since Nov 23 (each passed on retry).
- `check_logprobs_close` stays strict (top-5, no tolerance), so the test still catches a wrongly tied `lm_head` on the last PP stage.
- Test-only, one parameter, same on every platform (no ROCm branch).

## Validation

Failure on main, [build 105069](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/105069#01a20798-f736-41e4-afb4-db421cd61dfb):

```
FAILED distributed/test_pipeline_parallel.py::test_pp_tied_word_embeddings[granite4_h] - RuntimeError: Test subprocess 'test_pp_tied_word_embeddings' failed (exit code 1):
E               AssertionError: Test6:
E               Matched tokens:	[17, 13]
E               pp1:	'2. Explain the cultural significance of the'	{83017: Logprob(logprob=-2.2410080432891846, rank=1, decoded_token=' Explain'), 3639: Logprob(logprob=-2.4910080432891846, rank=2, decoded_token=' What'), 2650: Logprob(logprob=-2.4910080432891846, rank=3, decoded_token=' How'), 38527: Logprob(logprob=-2.4910080432891846, rank=4, decoded_token=' Analy'), 3146: Logprob(logprob=-2.4910080432891846, rank=5, decoded_token=' **')}
E               pp2:	'2. Discuss the role of the Mona'	{66379: Logprob(logprob=-2.2678627967834473, rank=2, decoded_token=' Discuss'), 83017: Logprob(logprob=-2.2678627967834473, rank=1, decoded_token=' Explain'), 38527: Logprob(logprob=-2.5178627967834473, rank=3, decoded_token=' Analy'), 3639: Logprob(logprob=-2.5178627967834473, rank=4, decoded_token=' What'), 2650: Logprob(logprob=-2.5178627967834473, rank=5, decoded_token=' How')}
```

Other failures on main: [105090](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/105090#01a2082b-5756-402f-80e1-4c5ed650cbd1), [105120](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/105120#01a208b1-de16-49ee-bcfd-57db7a86d6d9), [105315](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/105315#01a20c77-f7d2-4be2-a8e0-1b4b9b951998), [105605](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/105605#01a210de-6155-4c2d-b760-fd66a79375db), [105626](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/105626#01a2113c-c1ba-4eb4-8297-0517e89d7d85).

With this PR, MI250 (gfx90a), CI image `rocm/vllm-ci:test-deps-rocm-099b3d7ddfd89a4c`, 4 GPUs visible:

- `514c7c3edf` (this PR): 2/2 passed, `1 passed, 17 warnings in 75.27s (0:01:15)` and `1 passed, 17 warnings in 77.66s (0:01:17)`.
- `632ba4f90c` (no changes to the test, Granite or `LogitsProcessor` since): 20/20 passed, 74-78 s each, e.g. `1 passed, 17 warnings in 76.87s (0:01:16)`.

Not run on NVIDIA (no hardware). The L4 nightly step passed this test in all 6 nightlies since #67349 (105046 to 105646); the fp32 head takes the same `torch.mm(out_dtype=torch.float32)` path on CUDA and ROCm.

## Details

Root cause:

- Granite divides the logits by `logits_scaling=3` after the bf16 `lm_head`, so the top candidates land on a 0.25 grid (all logprobs above are -2.241/-2.491 or -2.268/-2.518). ` Explain` and ` Discuss` are really ~0.13 apart (fp32 head: -2.18 vs -2.31), so in bf16 they round to a gap of 0 or 0.25.
- MI250 is not batch-invariant, so pp1 and pp2 differ by ~0.03, enough to cross a rounding boundary. On a tie greedy picks the lower id (` Discuss`), and a 4-way tie at -2.491 pushes it out of pp1's top-5.

L4 runs this test nightly only and showed no pp1/pp2 divergence in 6/6 nightlies; MI250 diverged in 5/6.

Limitation: fp32 removes the artificial ties, not MI250's non-determinism. Genuine near-ties still swap in some runs, but the swapped token was always rank 2 and at least 0.39 above the 5th logprob.

Not taken: `near_tie_tol` (loosens the check).

AI assistance.

## Overview `Emu3Processor` prepends the BOS itself because its tokenizer doesn't, so multi-modal prompts for `BAAI/Emu3-Chat-hf` (served only through the Transformers modeling backend) lose it when vLLM tokenizes them. The backend now finds the tokens the HF processor puts in front of the tokenizer's ids and prepends them in `_postprocess_prompt`, as native Molmo2 does, which turns the Emu3 `xfail` in `test_spliced_prompt_matches_hf_expansion` (#51827, #60623) into a pass. ## Claims - Emu3's multi-modal prompts, chat path included, now have the same token ids as the HF processor's. - As in native Molmo2, token prompts and `add_special_tokens=False` requests get the prefix too (a token prompt gives the same ids as the text prompt), and a prompt that already starts with it keeps a single BOS (4173 ids) where `Emu3Processor` adds a second (4174). - Of the 24 processors I loaded, only Emu3 and Molmo2 get a prefix (list below). ## Validation ```bash pytest tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_transformers_image.py::test_spliced_prompt_matches_hf_expansion -k Emu3 ``` CPU, Transformers 5.24.1: - main's code (`git checkout e4ac319d20 -- vllm/model_executor/models/transformers/multimodal.py` on this branch): `1 failed, 3 deselected, 1 warning in 6.60s` (`At index 0 diff: 151852 != 151849`, `Right contains one more item: 1467`) - PR `7384887256`: `1 passed, 3 deselected, 1 warning in 13.36s` The rest of the backend's processing tests give the same results on main and the PR (summaries below). GB10, `LLM(model_impl="transformers")` greedy on Emu3-Chat-hf, chat with an image: the PR's prompt and output match Transformers' (4317 ids, 28/28 tokens); main's match Transformers fed the prompt without its BOS (details below). ## Details Text-only requests skip the multi-modal processor (`BaseRenderer._process_tokens`), so Emu3 still gets no BOS without an image, as with native Molmo2 (the `== text:` block of the GB10 output). I left that to the Hub and Transformers: it takes the three changes below, after which the probe finds nothing. The alternative is to apply `_postprocess_prompt` to text-only prompts in the renderer, a change to the shared path that also affects native Molmo and Molmo2.
What an upstream-only fix needs - `add_bos_token: true` in Emu3's `tokenizer_config.json`, for raw prompts. - A chat template that emits `{{ bos_token }}`, since chat requests are tokenized with `add_special_tokens=False`. - `Emu3Processor` no longer prepending when its tokenizer already does: with the flag alone it gives `[151849, 151849, 64]` for `"a"`. It ignores `add_special_tokens=False` today (`prepare_inputs_layout` reads a top-level kwarg that `__call__` nests under `text_kwargs`). - With all three, this probe finds nothing for Emu3. Once `Emu3Processor` honours `add_special_tokens=False`, the Emu3 case's reference call here (which passes it) loses the BOS, so that Transformers change needs the reference changed with it. - #51827 expected huggingface/transformers#47924 to fix the Emu3 case; it didn't, because vLLM tokenizes the prompt itself. - Molmo2's prepend is likewise a Transformers TODO waiting on the open allenai Hub PRs (allenai/Molmo2-8B#11, Molmo2-4B#4, Molmo2-O-7B#2).
Test level, and when no prefix is found - The prompt ids are decided in the multi-modal processor and nothing after `prompt_token_ids` changes, so this processor test is the cheapest level that reproduces the bug. There is no `LLM`-level CI test: Emu3-Chat-hf (8.8B parameters) is the only checkpoint that reaches this through the backend today (Molmo2 needs #69995), against the 0.3B–4B checkpoints of the backend's generation tests; the `LLM` check is the GB10 run below. - A processor that rejects a text-only call (PaliGemma needs images, Qwen3-ASR audio) gets no prefix.
GB10: Emu3-Chat-hf through LLM vs Transformers GB10 (sm_121), torch/CUDA from the image (2.14.0+cu130), vLLM `a87e3a6554` (+ #66840) with and without this change's two methods (the probe at an earlier revision, which returns the same prefix for Emu3), Transformers 5.24.1, bf16, `enforce_eager`, greedy, at most 48 tokens: ```python llm = LLM(model="BAAI/Emu3-Chat-hf", revision="414c0a163e", model_impl="transformers", dtype="bfloat16", max_model_len=20480, enforce_eager=True) llm.chat([{"role": "user", "content": [image_url, {"type": "text", "text": "Describe this image in one sentence."}]}], SamplingParams(temperature=0, max_tokens=48, logprobs=1)) ``` The image is vLLM's `cherry_blossom` asset at 640x427; the text-only request is "What is the capital of France? Answer in one sentence.". HF without the first token: ' The image captures a striking juxtaposition of nature and urban architecture, with a clear blue sky providing a serene backdrop to the delicate pink blossoms of a cherry blossom tree in the foreground, and a distinctive tower rising in the background.' commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Transformers backend] Don't split checkpoint tensors of skipped modules
commits.pr_body:
## Overview When the Transformers backend skips a module, #69695's `SplitWeights` raises on that module's fused checkpoint tensors instead of leaving them for the loader to drop: with `model_impl="transformers"`, Qianfan-OCR's vision `attn.qkv` hits this on pipeline ranks after the first or with `limit_mm_per_prompt={"image": 0}`. I pass the weights of skipped modules through unsplit. Reproducer (GB10, main's Transformers backend): ```python LLM("baidu/Qianfan-OCR", revision="623bf5d20d446abdb36606aa4547cd0c18886fe5", model_impl="transformers", limit_mm_per_prompt={"image": 0}) ``` ```text ValueError: Cannot split 'vision_model.encoder.layers.0.attn.qkv.bias' into ['attention.q_proj.bias', 'attention.k_proj.bias', 'attention.v_proj.bias']: 'model.vision_tower.layers.0.attention.q_proj.bias' is not a tensor of the model. Splitting quantized tensors is not supported. ``` This conflicts with my #69995, which rewrites `SplitWeights` as `ConvertWeights` and fails the same way (`Cannot convert 'model.vision_tower.layers.0.attn.qkv.bias' ...`). Either can land first; I'll rebase the other and keep the check and its test case. ## Claims - `baidu/Qianfan-OCR` loads with images disabled, and on both ranks with `pipeline_parallel_size=2`. With images enabled, the engine still fails at startup in the backend's multimodal processor, on main and with this PR (GB10 table below). - With images disabled, it generates the same greedy tokens as vLLM's native Qianfan-OCR. ## Validation The new case in `test_split_weights_splits_fused_gqa_qkv` fails on main and passes with this PR (CPU, below). With this PR, the real checkpoint loads with images disabled and on pipeline rank 1 of 2 (both fail on main); on GB10, its images-disabled `LLM` output matches vLLM native on 3/3 prompts. ## Details - **#64987 (open):** it drops other ranks' and skipped modules' weights before the weight transforms, but only when every transform in the mapper is a `RankLocalTransform`, and `SplitWeights` isn't one. - **Not reusing `get_pp_missing_layer_names`:** it caches by `id(model)`. Calling it when `SplitWeights` is built, before `pipeline_parallel()`, would store the pre-PP list for later callers.
Test (CPU, Transformers 5.24.1, main 7bca9fafe2, this PR d29ca6fce0) ```bash pytest tests/models/transformers/test_backend.py -k split_weights_splits_fused_gqa_qkv ``` ```text # main, with this PR's test file E ValueError: Cannot split 'vision_model.query_key_value.weight' into ['q_proj', 'k_proj', 'v_proj']: 'vision_tower.q_proj.weight' is not a tensor of the model. Splitting quantized tensors is not supported. 1 failed, 47 deselected, 1 warning in 1.73s # this PR 1 passed, 47 deselected, 1 warning in 6.02s ```
Real checkpoint: baidu/Qianfan-OCR at 623bf5d20d, CPU, bf16, model_loader.get_model, main 85a084c38c vs this PR These and the GB10 runs below are from before the rebase onto `7bca9fafe2`, with this head's `base.py`. ```text # main, limit_mm_per_prompt={"image": 0} rank0 FAILED: ValueError: Cannot split 'vision_model.encoder.layers.0.attn.qkv.bias' into ['attention.q_proj.bias', 'attention.k_proj.bias', 'attention.v_proj.bias']: 'model.vision_tower.layers.0.attention.q_proj.bias' is not a tensor of the model. Splitting quantized tensors is not supported. # this PR, limit_mm_per_prompt={"image": 0} rank0 loaded; skipped: ['model.vision_tower'] # main, pipeline_parallel_size=2, images enabled rank0 loaded; skipped: ['model.language_model.layers.18', ..., 'model.language_model.norm', 'lm_head'] rank1 FAILED: ValueError: Cannot split 'vision_model.encoder.layers.0.attn.qkv.bias' into [...]: 'model.vision_tower.layers.0.attention.q_proj.bias' is not a tensor of the model. Splitting quantized tensors is not supported. # this PR, pipeline_parallel_size=2, images enabled rank0 loaded; skipped: ['model.language_model.layers.18', ..., 'model.language_model.norm', 'lm_head'] rank1 loaded; skipped: ['model.vision_tower', 'model.language_model.embed_tokens', 'model.language_model.layers.0', ..., 'model.language_model.layers.17'] ```
GB10 (sm_121), torch 2.14.0+cu130, Transformers e35e1a5087, bf16, vllm.LLM These runs use vLLM a87e3a6554 with main's Transformers backend package (`85a084c38c`), or with this PR's `base.py`. `baidu/Qianfan-OCR` at `623bf5d20d`, `enforce_eager=True`, greedy, 32 tokens. | run | result | |---|---| | main, `limit_mm_per_prompt={"image": 0}` | the `ValueError` above | | this PR, `limit_mm_per_prompt={"image": 0}` | 3/3 prompts identical to vLLM native (8/8, 32/32, 32/32 tokens); max \|Δ logprob\| 0.12 | | main and this PR, images enabled | both fail before generating, in the backend's multimodal processor (`Failed to apply QianfanOCRProcessor`): its dummy text uses `image_token` (``), while this processor counts ``. commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Keep the most likely candidate's logprob when /v1/completions top_logprobs keys collide
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

`/v1/completions` keys `top_logprobs` by decoded string, so when candidates decode to the same string (byte fragments all decode to `""`), the last one in engine order overwrites the sampled token's entry and `top_logprobs[i][tokens[i]] != token_logprobs[i]`. This PR keeps the highest logprob among the candidates that share a string in both `/v1/completions` and `/v1/completions/derender`. A tie keeps the earlier candidate, which is the sampled token.

Fixes #65726

## Claims

- In `/v1/completions` (streaming and non-streaming, including echoed prompt positions), `top_logprobs[i][tokens[i]] == token_logprobs[i]` now holds whenever the token at that position is the most likely of the candidates that share its string. That includes every greedy position, so it covers every case in #65726. On main it breaks when a later candidate shares the token's string.
- `max(top_logprobs[i].values())` is now the logprob of the most likely returned candidate wherever `top_logprobs[i]` is not `None`, so a greedy check that reads it (as lm-evaluation-harness does) sees the text of the most likely returned candidate.
- Barring exact ties between different candidates, no position is worse than on main for either check. Main keeps the token's own entry only when no other candidate shares its string, and then this PR keeps it too.
- `/v1/completions/derender` returns the same `top_logprobs` as the coupled endpoint for these positions.
- Only the value of a colliding key changes. Keys, key order, entry count, `tokens` and `text_offset` are the same as before in all cases.

## Validation

Environment for the unit tests and CPU checks: CPU only, aarch64, Python 3.12, torch 2.14.0+cpu, transformers 5.21.1, tokenizers 0.23.3. vLLM is a Python-only editable install with this branch first on `PYTHONPATH`. No compiled ops are needed.

**Server tests.** `test_top_logprobs_keep_sampled_entry_on_string_collision` and its `_stream` variant in `tests/entrypoints/openai/completion/test_completion.py` use the module's existing `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B` `RemoteOpenAIServer`. They are deterministic: `allowed_token_ids=[8158]` forces the sampled token to a leading-byte fragment of U+0E58 (Thai digit 8), and `logprob_token_ids=[3023, 378]` requests two other leading fragments. After `Hello`, 8158 is the most likely of the three (fp32 forward pass on CPU: -14.21, against -15.04 for 378 and -15.35 for 3023), so the highest value is the sampled token's own. All three decode to `""`, so the position has one `""` key, and the tests assert that its value is `token_logprobs[0]`. They compare the two returned values rather than fixed floats, and they do not set `return_tokens_as_token_ids` (with it, the keys are `token_id:N` and nothing collides). The "Entrypoints Integration (OpenAI API completion)" CI step runs them (`pytest -v -s entrypoints/openai/completion`). Under the Rust frontend (`VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1`) they are skipped with `pytest.mark.skipif` until #68488 (the Rust follow-up) and #63926 land.

```bash
pytest -v -s tests/entrypoints/openai/completion/test_completion.py -k string_collision
```

On a DGX Spark (GB10, aarch64), at bb10b60c3 (the earlier first-wins revision; not rerun for highest-wins, which keeps the same entry here because 8158 is the most likely of the three), with this branch installed from source on a `VLLM_USE_PRECOMPILED=1` cu130 wheel (torch 2.14.0+cu130, `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B`, `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.10` added by a local wrapper because GB10 memory is shared with the host):

```text
with this PR:
tests/entrypoints/openai/completion/test_completion.py::test_top_logprobs_keep_sampled_entry_on_string_collision PASSED
tests/entrypoints/openai/completion/test_completion.py::test_top_logprobs_keep_sampled_entry_on_string_collision_stream PASSED
2 passed, 25 deselected

with the fix reverted (git checkout HEAD~1 -- vllm/entrypoints/openai/completion/serving.py vllm/renderers/online_derenderer.py):
E       AssertionError: assert [{'': -15.044697761535645}] == [{'': -14.21267318725586}]   (non-stream)
E       AssertionError: assert [{'': -15.044697761535645}] == [{'': -14.21267318725586}]   (stream)
2 failed, 25 deselected
```

Before the fix, the `""` key carries the logprob of token 378 (-15.04) instead of the sampled token 8158's own value (-14.21).

**Unit test.** `test_completion_top_logprobs_keeps_highest_entry_on_string_collision` in `tests/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/test_logprobs_endpoint_parity.py` builds the per-position dicts with the engine's own `LogprobsProcessor._update_sample_logprobs`, so the U+FFFD correction turns the fragments into `""` exactly as in serving. It then checks the coupled `_create_completion_logprobs` output, and checks that derender matches it. At its third position the sampled token (-1.5) has rank 2 behind a colliding candidate (-0.5), and the test expects `{"": -0.5}`. It uses the `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B` tokenizer only (no weights). It is the only test that covers derender parity.

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES= VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 \
  .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/test_logprobs_endpoint_parity.py -v
```

Before, with main's (952dc48bcf) two source files and this branch's tests:

```bash
git checkout upstream/main -- vllm/entrypoints/openai/completion/serving.py vllm/renderers/online_derenderer.py && \
  CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES= VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 \
  .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/test_logprobs_endpoint_parity.py -v
```

```text
E   AssertionError: assert [{' ': -0.25, '': -14.0}, {'': -14.0}, {'': -14.0}] == [{' ': -0.25, '': -12.25}, {'': -0.5}, {'': -0.5}]
E     At index 0 diff: {' ': -0.25, '': -14.0} != {' ': -0.25, '': -12.25}
FAILED ...::test_completion_top_logprobs_keeps_highest_entry_on_string_collision
1 failed, 17 passed
```

With the coupled fix only, the derender comparison fails (`'top_logprobs': [{' ': -0.25, '': -14.0}, {'': -14.0}, {'': -14.0}]` vs `[{' ': -0.25, '': -12.25}, {'': -0.5}, {'': -0.5}]`). That failure is why both builders are changed. With first-wins in both builders (the previous revision), the third position fails: `{'': -1.5} != {'': -0.5}`.

With this PR: `18 passed`.

<details>
<summary>Surrounding suites, with and without the fix</summary>

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES= VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  tests/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/test_logprobs_endpoint_parity.py \
  tests/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/test_generate_logprobs_conversion.py \
  tests/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/test_derender.py \
  tests/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/test_derender_stream.py \
  tests/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/test_derender_parity.py \
  tests/entrypoints/openai/completion/test_completion_error.py \
  tests/entrypoints/openai/completion/test_completion_text_offset.py \
  tests/entrypoints/openai/completion/test_stream_frame_template.py \
  tests/v1/engine/test_logprobs_processor.py
```

| | passed | failed | xfailed | errors |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| main's source files | 267 | 1 (the new test) | 1 | 154 |
| this PR | 268 | 0 | 1 | 154 |

The 154 errors are the same on both sides. 109 are the server-backed `test_e2e_*` / streaming round-trip tests, which spawn the `vllm` CLI. It is not installed on PATH in this Python-only editable environment (`FileNotFoundError: 'vllm'`). The other 45 are in `test_derender_parity.py`, whose `DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B` weights are not in the local cache. These tests run in the "Entrypoints Integration (API Server)" CI step, which already selects `tests/entrypoints/scale_out`.

</details>

`pre-commit run --files` on the five changed files (`uvx pre-commit`): ruff check, ruff format, typos, check-test-tethering, mypy, check-spdx-header, check-root-lazy-imports, check-filenames, update-dockerfile-graph, check-forbidden-imports, check-torch-cuda-call, validate-config, check-dockerignore-tracked, check-boolean-context-manager, check-docstring-style and check-trust-remote-code passed. The other hooks were skipped because no matching files changed.

**Real engine, before and after.** DGX Spark (GB10), `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.25.1-aarch64` serving `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B` (`--enforce-eager --seed 0`), `/v1/completions`, `logprobs=3`, `temperature=0`, `max_tokens=24`, stream and non-stream. The second run bind-mounts the image's `completion/serving.py` with the first-wins change of the previous revision backported (0.25.1 predates the `completion_top_logprobs_limit` refactor, so this is the equivalent one-hunk change, not this branch's file). The check is `top_logprobs[i][tokens[i]] == token_logprobs[i]` at every position:

| prompt | positions with an `""` token or candidate | mismatches, 0.25.1 | mismatches, 0.25.1 + fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ปี พ.ศ. ๒๕๖๙ ตรงกับปี ค.ศ.` (Thai digits) | 6 / 24 (stream 5) | 3 non-stream, 3 stream | 0, 0 |
| `นับเลขไทยจาก ๑ ถึง ๙:` | 12 / 24 | 0, 0 | 0, 0 |
| `Three emojis for a party: ` | 9 / 24 | 8 non-stream, 8 stream | 0, 0 |

Generated text is identical in both runs. Example mismatch before the fix: `token='' token_logprob=-0.0035` but `top_logprobs={'': -7.44}`.

Limits of this run: it used the first-wins rule of the previous revision. At `temperature=0` the sampled token is the most likely candidate, so highest-wins keeps the same entries, but it was not rerun. It also did not call `/v1/completions/derender`, and 0.25.1 has no `logprob_token_ids` on completions, so the derender change is covered only by the unit parity test above, and this branch's own `serving.py` was not served there. The GB10 `RemoteOpenAIServer` run above covers the coupled path at bb10b60c3 (stream and non-stream).

<details>
<summary>Original report: Qwen3-8B-NVFP4 on 0.25.1</summary>

vLLM 0.25.1 (`vllm/vllm-openai:v0.25.1-aarch64`) on the same DGX Spark, `nvidia/Qwen3-8B-NVFP4`, `/v1/completions`, `logprobs=3`, `temperature=0`, before the fix:

- the prompt `"ตัวเลขไทย: ๑ ๒ ๓ ๔ ๕ ๖ ๗"` was affected at 4 of 24 positions. At position 1, token 8158 had `token_logprob=-4.41e-05` but `top_logprobs={"": -12.25}`: the `""` key carried a less likely candidate's value instead of the sampled token's. With the fix the key carries the sampled token's own value; the 8B model was not rerun (the 0.6B runs above were);
- the prompt `"อีโมจิ: 🙏🏻 🇹🇭 🫨 💪🏾"` was affected at 7 of 24 positions;
- the streaming responses from the same run show the same pattern (4 of 24 and 8 of 24 positions).

</details>

No model evaluation: the change only affects how already-computed logprobs are reported. Sampling and generated text are unchanged.

## Details

**Root cause.** In the original report, a sampled byte fragment had `token_logprobs[i] = -4.4e-05` but `top_logprobs[i] = {"": -12.25}`. Both builders use `{decoded_token: logprob for each candidate}`. The engine row is the sampled token first, then the top-k by rank or the requested `logprob_token_ids` in request order (`append_logprobs_for_next_position`; `_get_sampled_context_ids` and the derender docstring rely on the same order). Python's dict keeps the first key position but the last value, so the last of several colliding candidates wins. Fragments become `""` in `LogprobsProcessor._correct_decoded_token` (#28874, #34875), which returns `""` when a token's bytes do not yet complete a character.

**Fix.** In `_create_completion_logprobs` and in `_convert_chat_logprobs_to_completion_logprobs`, keep the highest logprob per string, comparing with a strict `>` so a tie keeps the earlier candidate (the token at that position is always first). The dict comprehension becomes a loop; `_get_decoded_token`, the `-9999.0` clamp and the `completion_top_logprobs_limit` cut are unchanged.

The rule is a few lines in each builder. Their inputs differ (`dict[int, Logprob]` with decode and clamp, versus resolved chat entries), so I kept it inline. The parity test guards against drift: it fails with only the coupled builder changed.

**Limitation.** Colliding candidates still share one string key, so such a position still has fewer than `logprobs + 1` entries. This PR only fixes which value is kept. Clients that need every candidate can pass `return_tokens_as_token_ids=true`, or use chat completions, which returns a list. The description of `CompletionLogProbs.top_logprobs` in `vllm/entrypoints/openai/completion/protocol.py` says this, so it shows up in the OpenAPI schema.

**Alternatives considered.**
- Re-inserting only the sampled token's entry after the comprehension. It fixes the sampled entry, but other collisions would still keep the last value. Highest-wins covers both cases with one rule.
- First wins (the previous revision of this PR). It keeps the token's own entry wherever `top_logprobs[i]` is not `None`, but a more likely candidate with the same string is then hidden from `max(top_logprobs[i].values())`. tkhongsap's lm-eval run showed the greedy check getting worse with it at `logprobs=1` (0 to 4 wrong). Highest-wins differs from it only where a colliding candidate outranks the token, and main gets the token's entry wrong there too.
- Making the strings distinct, as #48674 did for SentencePiece spaces. A fragment has no printable form, and changing `""` would also change `tokens` and `text_offset`.

**Rust frontend.** `position_top_logprobs_map` in `rust/src/server/src/routes/openai/utils/logprobs.rs` mirrors the old Python rule on purpose (#63763: "the last value for it, like Python's dict"). Rust already has the same collision today. It decodes each candidate on its own, so byte fragments all become `"\ufffd"`, and the open #63926 makes them `""` like Python. Special tokens can also collide on `""` (#63917). Until a follow-up lands, the two frontends report different values for colliding strings, so the two `string_collision` tests are skipped when `VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND` is set, with a comment pointing at #68488 and #63926. The follow-up is #68488: the map keeps the highest logprob, with an `expect_test` case for candidates that decode to the same string. The skip can be removed once #68488 and #63926 are in.

**Why this is not a duplicate.**
- No open PR references #65726 (`gh pr list --state open --search "65726 in:body"`).
- #48674 (fixes #44319) handled SentencePiece space-stripping collisions in `convert_ids_list_to_tokens`. It does not cover byte fragments, which still decode to `""` on main.
- #36746 deduplicates the sampled token in the engine's top-k by token id, not by string.
- #53722 changes the same function for a missing sampled token (`KeyError`). It does not overlap with this change and may need a trivial rebase.
- #61982 changes the U+FFFD correction for tokens that start with continuation bytes and then contain more text. Pure leading fragments still decode to `""`.

<summary>Searches run</summary>

`gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search` for "top_logprobs", "_create_completion_logprobs", "logprobs collision" and "top_logprobs empty"; issue searches for "top_logprobs empty string", "top_logprobs overwritten", "logprobs token string collision" and "top_logprobs fewer entries". None of the open PRs changes how the string-keyed dict is built.

</details>

**AI assistance.** AI assistance (Claude) was used to find the bug in the GB10 test logs, write the CPU reproduction, the fix and the tests, and draft this description. I reviewed every changed line; the tests and the GB10 runs above were run on my machine.

commits.pr_title: [Perf][DCP] Size sparse-indexer decode logits by the DCP-local context
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Size sparse-indexer decode logits for each DCP rank's local KV context rather than the full model context. This frees CUDA graph memory for KV cache without changing global top-k indices.

## Claims

- With localized decode metadata, allocate at most `ceil(max_model_len / (DCP * interleave)) * interleave` columns. The profile reservation uses the same bound; PCP profiling and non-localized decode retain the global width.
- The supplied Kimi K3.1 Pro A/B measured 2.19 GiB less CUDA graph memory per rank and 5.9% more KV blocks on TP8/DCP8 across two nodes with four GB300 GPUs each.
- No flags or defaults change, and no throughput or capacity benchmark claim is made.

## Validation

**Local checks:** commit `7ed49b2203f249959a60f24897eb37e450d2676a`, based on upstream `a95fbda2c`.

```sh
pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/model_executor/layers/sparse_attn_indexer.py \
  tests/v1/attention/test_indexer_dcp_localize.py
```

All applicable hooks pass, including mypy and CI test tethering. The added 36 cases live in the existing `V1 Attention` suite, selected by `pytest -v -s v1/attention`; that step already lists the changed runtime file as a source dependency.

The new cases exercise the real width helper and `get_dcp_local_seq_lens` over every global length up to the configured maximum, DCP 1/2/4/8, interleave 1/16/64, and maximum lengths 1/127/100003. They check shard coverage, tight bounds, and the memory reduction.

On macOS, an isolated harness executed those unchanged test bodies and source-extracted production functions with torch 2.15.0, avoiding CUDA/Triton imports:

```text
36 passed in 0.04s
```

Using the original global allocation width in the same diagnostic:

```text
15 failed, 21 passed in 0.08s
```

These are source-level diagnostics, not a normal vLLM pytest run. To run the contributed tests in a supported vLLM environment:

```sh
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -v -s \
  tests/v1/attention/test_indexer_dcp_localize.py \
  -k test_decode_logits_width_covers_local_contexts
```

**Previously recorded GPU validation of the same runtime patch:** nightly `c2cc003c5b644095cabcd5212d2967546ce344f8`, Kimi K3.1 Pro, TP8/DCP8, two nodes with four GB300 GPUs each, maximum model length 1,048,576, FULL decode graphs, 128 sequences, four speculative tokens. One boot per arm; different node pairs. Both arms included the same two unrelated overlays for MoE workspace sizing and DCP prefill limits.

| Per rank | Base | With this runtime patch |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| CUDA graph pool | 9.10 GiB | 6.91 GiB |
| KV cache blocks | 3551 | 3762 |
| GPU KV cache tokens | 17,399,501 | 18,433,378 |

The recorded check recomputed global-width and local-width logits during the first four decode steps of a 95k-token request on all eight ranks: 32/32 comparisons were bit-identical, including all five top-k rows. That request and three additional 36k-token requests returned HTTP 200 with correct continuations. These measurements are supplied evidence, not fresh GPU runs on this PR head.

The original bundle also reported 13/13 tests passing for its earlier test file, and 156 existing CPU tests passing with 201 CUDA-only skips on both arms. This PR replaces that earlier mocked test file with the concise cases in the existing DCP suite; those earlier counts do not describe the new test file.

**Limits:** no fresh GPU run or full endpoint validation suite was performed for this PR. The supplied GPU correctness probes reach about 95k global tokens / 11.9k local tokens; contexts above the 131k local allocation width, XPU hardware, and production offload pressure were not exercised. No model accuracy benchmark or throughput comparison is included. Full launch commands and raw GPU logs are not available in the supplied PR bundle; the recorded configuration and comparisons above are the available evidence.

## Details

The decode metadata builder already converts sequence lengths to each rank's local context. DeepGEMM therefore writes only the local shard, but previously retained a full `max_model_len`-wide logits buffer inside every captured decode graph. At 1M context and 640 speculative decode rows, DeepGEMM's padded FP32 allocation drops from approximately 2.50 to 0.31 GiB per rank at DCP8.

The runtime change adds a shared bound helper, applies it to CUDA/XPU decode only when `global_seq_lens` indicates localization, and uses it for profiling unless PCP is active. DCP merging still uses the full model length to reconstruct global indices. The change adds no GPU host reads or synchronization.

DeepGEMM requires the width to cover every local context. Persistent and sampled top-k paths clamp their reads to the buffer; cooperative top-k uses its stride, and DeepGEMM preserves the required alignment. The DCP merge packs candidates using the actual logits shape and stride.

Duplicate checks on 2026-11-26 found no open PR implementing this DCP-local decode bound. Related #62169 chunks non-DCP decode requests and explicitly retains DCP's full-batch path. #58068 changes prefill allocation, and #42856 changes SM120 workspace bounds. These solve different allocation problems.

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Serve /v1/decisions with next-token reads
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Serve the Decisions API (`/v1/decisions`) in the Rust frontend for checkpoints that Python reads with `NextTokenStrategy` (Qwen3, Qwen3.5, Gemma 4): the "Decisions API" item of #68784. `/v1/systemone` follows in a separate PR.

## Claims

- `/v1/decisions` answers predicate, choice and score questions with the probabilities, confidences and usage of the Python frontend, except `cached_tokens` on hybrid models (see Details). Each question is one greedy one-token read with thinking off, scored from the option labels' logprobs.
- Python's `select_read_strategy` stays the only table of supported models: the launcher forwards the class name of the strategy it picks in `--args-json` (`decisions_read_strategy`), and nothing where Python answers 501. The Rust frontend implements `NextTokenStrategy` and refuses any other name at startup, so the Rust frontend on e.g. `Qwen3_5ForSlotDecision` fails at launch instead of answering 501. It probes the chat template at startup as `NextTokenStrategy.__init__` does; without a strategy, or when the probe fails, the endpoint answers 501 as before.
- The Rust frontend CI step runs `test_decisions_e2e.py` (without its `/v1/systemone` cases).

Not a duplicate: no open PR implements the Decisions API in the Rust frontend; #68654 (closed) put the Python one behind a flag.

## Validation

At `62d5ec32ea`:

```text
$ cd rust && cargo nextest run -p vllm-server -p vllm-cmd -p vllm-text -p vllm-llm
     Summary [   6.864s] 1091 tests run: 1091 passed, 1 skipped
$ pytest tests/entrypoints/launchers/api_server/test_api_server_process_manager.py -k decisions_read_strategy
7 passed, 25 deselected, 16 warnings in 1.02s
```

The prompts and the label softmax match Python's `question_types.py` byte for byte and bit for bit in unit tests.

End to end on one GB200, at `ce06978522`, before the review changes (only how the strategy reaches the frontend) and the rebase onto main; not rerun since: Qwen3-0.6B with `test_decisions_e2e.py`'s server arguments, nightly wheel of 13c850cb6 plus this branch's launcher change and `vllm-rs`. The same 11 requests went to the Python and the Rust frontend:

| Requests | Result |
|---|---|
| The test file's request; bool and quoted choice values; message parts; 26 choices; 10 questions on a 7.4K-token input with `cache_salt` | Same answers and labels, probabilities equal within 2.3e-16, same input/output tokens (129/3, 65/1, 113/2, 162/1, 7419/10) and cached tokens |
| 27 choices, `joint`, 65 questions, repeated choice values, unknown model | Same status and message |
| An image part | 400 on both; the message wording differs (Pydantic vs serde) |

## Details

- The route lives next to `/generative_scoring` and shares its label-logprob reading. A read leaves `logprobs` unset, as in Python, so a choice may have more options than `--max-logprobs`.
- `vllm-chat` gets a synchronous `render` for the startup probe.
- #70020 (open) moves Python's score questions on `/v1/decisions` to the native score prompt; if it lands first, the mapping here follows it.
- Not yet ported: Python's shared-prefix warm-up (#61192). On hybrid models with prefix caching, Python prefills the reads' common prefix once before submitting them; here each read prefills it, which is slower for many questions on a long input and reports fewer `cached_tokens`. Marked with a TODO in `next_token.rs`; it follows in a separate PR.
- Differences from Python: there is no up-front admission check for all reads (`check_admission(n)`), as in `/generative_scoring`; reads are admitted one by one and the decision fails with 503 if one is rejected. Pydantic-level validation messages are worded differently.

## Purpose

Remove unused speculative scaffolding (`SleepModeState`, `_state` / `state()`, and 4 uncalled capability `@classmethod`s) from `vllm/device_allocator/sleep_mode_backend.py`.

- Sleep state is already authoritatively tracked by the engine/executor (`is_sleeping` / `sleeping_tags`) and allocator (`AllocationData.is_asleep`); `CuMemBackend._state` had zero callers and drifted on partial wakes (`resume(tags=["weights"])` unconditionally set `"RUNNING"`).
- `cuda-checkpoint` / snapshot landed on executor/session hooks (#51360 / #66567) rather than `SleepModeBackend`, leaving the four capability classmethods with zero production callers anywhere in `vllm/`.

## Changes

- `vllm/device_allocator/sleep_mode_backend.py` (`+1 / -51`, net `-50` LOC):
  - Remove `SleepModeState`, `SleepModeBackend.__init__` / `state()`, and `self._state` mutations in `CuMemBackend`.
  - Remove the 4 uncalled capability `@classmethod`s: `preserves_communicators`, `preserves_compiled_artifacts`, `preserves_graphs_with_communicators`, and `supports_durable_storage`.
  - Keep all active `SleepModeBackend` / `CuMemBackend` / `SleepModeBackendFactory` APIs (`suspend`, `resume`, `discard`, `is_supported`, registration/creation) unchanged.
- `tests/v1/worker/test_sleep_mode_backend.py` (`+6 / -33`, net `-27` LOC):
